description: Conserved behavioral epitopes from automated scraping fleet. Published for community immunity. Any infrastructure operator can use these signatures for detection.

conserved_epitopes.name: header_poverty
conserved_epitopes.description: Missing Sec-Fetch-Mode header. Mandatory in all Chromium browsers since Chrome 76 (July 2019). Absence proves the client is not a browser.
conserved_epitopes.detection: Count HTTP headers per request. Fleet sends 3. Chrome sends 11+. Firefox sends 8+.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Must implement full browser header stack — fundamentally changes the scraping toolkit.

conserved_epitopes.name: stale_chrome
conserved_epitopes.description: User-Agent claims Chrome/150 but current stable is Chrome/155. Real Chrome auto-updates. Hardcoded UA string proves automation.
conserved_epitopes.detection: Parse Chrome major version from User-Agent. Compare to current stable release.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Must implement UA version tracking — reveals the UA is dynamically generated, not from a real browser.

conserved_epitopes.name: connection_absent
conserved_epitopes.description: No Connection: keep-alive header. Chrome always sends this header. Absence proves the client is not Chrome.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Trivial to add — but adding it while missing other headers increases detection confidence.

conserved_epitopes.name: content_gate
conserved_epitopes.description: Over 50% of requests target /commit/, /src/, /raw/, /blame/ paths. Source code extraction, not browsing.
conserved_epitopes.detection: Calculate ratio of requests to code-hosting paths vs. all paths.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Must add noise requests to non-code paths — increases bandwidth cost and detection surface.

conserved_epitopes.name: accept_monoculture
conserved_epitopes.description: Universal */* Accept header. Real browsers send resource-specific Accept headers (text/html for pages, image/webp for images, etc.).
conserved_epitopes.detection: Check if Accept header is exactly '*/*' for HTML page requests.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Must implement resource-type-aware Accept headers — requires understanding page context.

conserved_epitopes.name: blame_ratio
conserved_epitopes.description: Over 10% of requests target /blame/ paths. Author attribution mining — mapping who wrote every line of code.
conserved_epitopes.detection: Calculate ratio of /blame/ requests to total requests per behavioral subgroup.
conserved_epitopes.evasion_cost: Cannot be avoided if the goal is author attribution data.

detection_rules.description: Any system exhibiting 4 or more of these rules simultaneously is this fleet.
rules: User-Agent contains 'Chrome/' but Sec-Fetch-Mode header is ABSENT
User-Agent contains 'Chrome/' but Sec-Ch-Ua header is ABSENT
Chrome major version is 5+ behind current stable
Accept-Encoding is identical across >90% of population
Accept-Language is identical across >90% of population
>80% of IPs make exactly 1 request (single-page rotation)

timing_signature.description: Inter-request timing distribution. 99.3% of requests arrive at 0.0-0.1 second intervals.
